title: Tenali and the Royal Sword of State
summary: The ceremonial Sword of State—a magnificent damascene steel blade encrusted with rubies, gifted to King Krishnadevaraya by the King of Kalinga—disappeared overnight from the sec...
keywords: tenali and the sword of the king
full_text:
The ceremonial Sword of State—a magnificent damascene steel blade encrusted with rubies, gifted to King Krishnadevaraya by the King of Kalinga—disappeared overnight from the secure armory inside the citadel.
The iron door showed no signs of forced entry, indicating that one of the four night sentries on duty had committed the theft.

All four guards—Ramu, Somu, Bheemu, and Deva—swore upon their sacred daggers that they had seen nothing.
The King was on the verge of ordering them tortured when Tenali Raman intervened:
'Maharaj, violence only forces innocent men to confess falsehoods. Allow me to test the sentries using the ancient Turmeric Test of Kalinga.'

Tenali had the four guards assembled in a courtyard.
He brought forth a large stone basin filled with pure water mixed with crushed fresh turmeric roots, turning the water bright, radiant yellow.
Tenali announced:
'The ceremonial steel of Kalinga has a secret metallurgical property: it reacts with the human sweat of whoever touched it within forty-eight hours.
Wash your hands thoroughly in this yellow turmeric water. The innocent will see no change. But whoever touched the stolen blade will find that his hands turn bright crimson-red within five minutes!'

The four guards dipped their hands into the yellow water, washing vigorously.
Tenali then handed each man a clean linen towel to dry his hands.
Three of the towels showed only yellow turmeric stains.

However, Tenali noticed that the fourth guard, Bheemu, was repeatedly rubbing his palms against his woolen trousers, nervously checking his fingers.
Tenali suddenly stepped forward and touched Bheemu’s wet hands with a piece of wet alkaline lime paste (*chunam*), used for betel leaves!
The chemical reaction between the alkaline lime and the turmeric immediately turned Bheemu’s wet hands bright, blood-red!

Bheemu shrieked in horror, falling to his knees:
'The blade has cursed me! I confess! I hid the Sword of State inside the hollow stone cannon on the north rampart!'

The guards ran to the rampart and recovered the precious sword undamaged.
The King marveled at Tenali’s demonstration.
Tenali smiled:
'Maharaj, turmeric naturally turns red when touched with alkaline lime; the only magic was in the thief's own panic, which revealed his guilt!'
Bheemu was punished, the innocent sentries were exonerated, and Tenali’s forensic wit preserved justice.
moral: A thief cannot hide physical evidence when confronted with chemical truth.
